Thought: Let me analyze the reaction between carboxylic acids and cyanide salts. Carboxylic acids (RCOOH) are weak acids that can donate a proton (H+). Cyanide salts (like NaCN or KCN) contain the cyanide ion (CN-). When these two react, the acid will donate a proton to the cyanide ion, forming hydrogen cyanide (HCN) gas. This is actually a dangerous reaction because hydrogen cyanide is highly toxic.

The reaction would be:
RCOOH + CN- → RCOO- + HCN

Looking at the options:
A. Ammonia and hydrogen gas - Not correct for this reaction
B. Hydrogen and carbon monoxide - Not correct for this reaction
C. Hydrogen cyanide - This matches the product of the reaction
D. Hydrogen sulfide and sulfur dioxide - These involve sulfur compounds, which aren't part of this reaction

The correct answer is C. Hydrogen cyanide.
